title: The Curious Case of Curiosity across Human Cultures and LLMs
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the alignment of LLM-generated curiosity with human curiosity across cultures. Religion was a factor within the 'Conservation' value of Schwartz's Cultural Values theory, which was computed based on the presence of religious and family-related terms ('relig + family').
findings: A human-authored example question about the Christian trinity and the bible indicated that religion is a topic of human curiosity. When grounding curiosity in social science theories, the paper found that both humans and LLaMA models showed little reflection of the stronger religious/traditional conservation values expected in Asian and Latin American countries, suggesting a flattening of this cultural dimension.
